claims.text: Subjects with NAFLD exhibit a 69% increased mortality compared to the general Swedish population.
Subjects with NASH exhibit an 86% increased mortality compared to the general Swedish population.
Subjects with nonalcoholic bland steatosis exhibit a 55% increased mortality compared to the general population, which was not statistically significant.
Liver disease is the third most common cause of death among patients with NAFLD.
Cardiovascular disease was the most frequent cause of death in the cohort, accounting for 37 of 113 deaths.

evidence.description: Compared with the total Swedish population, adjusted for sex, age, and calendar period, subjects with NAFLD exhibited a 69% increased mortality (SMR = 1.69; 95% CI, 1.24-2.25).
Subjects with NASH exhibited an 86% increased mortality (SMR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.19-2.76; P = 0.007).
Subjects with bland steatosis exhibited a 55% increase (SMR, 1.55; 95% CI, 0.98-2.32; P = 0.062).
Liver disease is the third most common cause of death among patients with NAFLD.
Of the 113 deaths, 37 were of cardiovascular disease and 16 of liver diseases.

methodologies.name: Longitudinal cohort mortality study
methodologies.description: A 28-year follow-up study of 256 subjects who underwent liver biopsy due to elevated liver enzymes, using registry-matched mortality data.
datasets: National Swedish Cause of Death Registry
conditions: Blind histological scoring for NAFLD and NASH
Adjustment for sex, age, and calendar period

limitations.text: Long-term survival of subjects with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in comparison with both individuals with elevated transaminases attributable to other causes and the general population was poorly characterized.
The 55% increased mortality observed in subjects with bland steatosis did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.062).
